title.narrative: Technical Oversight and Capacity Strengthening of NNGOs for Climate-Resilient Food Security Interventions in Jere and MMC Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtMalteser International (MI) is applying under Thematic Envelope 1: Climate Adaptation and Food Security of the NHF Third Standard Allocation to deliver a technical support and capacity-strengthening initiative that enhances the quality, accountability, and climate-resilient focus of food security interventions implemented by national NGOs (NNGOs) in MMC and Jere LGAs, Borno State. The NHF July 2025 Rapid Technical Capacity Mapping identified NNGOs as strong frontline actors with extensive experience across WASH, nutrition, livelihoods, protection, cash and voucher assistance (CVA), and community engagement. However, the assessment also highlighted critical gaps in technical and organization capacities of NNGOs, including in climate adaptation, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), compliance, financial oversight, and inclusive programming. These gaps limit their ability to meet NHF requirements, especially in nutrition-sensitive and climate-smart food security programming.ltbrgtUnder the proposed action, MI will address systemic capacity gaps and equip NNGOs with the tools, skills, and oversight required to implement effective and impactful nutrition-sensitive and climate-resilient food security interventions, thereby reducing vulnerability and contributing to resilience in line with the 2025 HNRP. MI brings substantial experience in nutrition-sensitive programming and climate-smart agriculture (CSA) from German Federal Foreign Office and Aktion Deutschland Hilft–funded initiatives, including the introduction of hydroponic fodder systems, solar tent dryers, biochar manure, solar-powered incubators, nutrient-rich crops, small-scale livestock systems, and improved food preparation and preservation practices. Aligned with NHF localisation commitments, MI will provide oversight, quality assurance, and structured capacity strengthening to NNGOs, without direct implementation or sub-granting. MI will lead trainings and technical support of NNGO staff in baseline and endline assessments, CSA and nutrition-sensitive food security, MEAL, compliance and digital reporting, as well as provide guidance on Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), gender equality, and disability inclusion. MI will ensure targeted NNGOs are employing robust monitoring and quality assurance mechanisms by implementing joint monitoring visits, digital dashboards, compliance checklists, and continuous technical mentoring. The proposed action will also strengthen linkages and coordination between NNGOs and government authorities, enhancing NNGO leadership and influence within the humanitarian response.ltbrgtlt/pgt
